overview: 1937 exchange: State asked whether Schuler's Kobe shipping-subsidy figures were official; Grew's reply, from Kobe, confirms they came unofficially from the Japan Shipping Exchange, explains construction-subsidy eligibility and 1938 mail-subsidy appropriations, and promises the new law and budget details by mail.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan and sender of the June 12 telegram from Tokyo

people.name: Schuler
people.role: U.S. Vice Consul; author of the shipping report dated April 22, 1937

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Department telegram No. 76 on Japanese shipping subsidies
subfiles.about: The sheet points to the Department’s inquiry about the calculations and legal basis for Japanese ship-construction and mail subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 76: State asks if Schuler's ship-price data were official and how subsidies applied by vessel type.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet summarizing Grew’s telegram No. 156
subfiles.about: The sheet summarizes the reply concerning the sources, availability, and appropriations for Japanese shipping subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 156: Grew confirms figures were unofficial but reliable, with details to follow by mail.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew transmitting Kobe’s answers on Japanese shipping subsidies
subfiles.about: Grew transmits the Kobe Consulate’s detailed answers to the Department’s questions about Japanese ship-construction and mail subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Kobe reports shipping figures came unofficially from the Japan Shipping Exchange; construction subsidies totaled ¥50,693,567 (mostly combination vessels), and 1938 mail subsidies totaled ¥9,550,736, with the new law to follow by mail.

interest: Shows 1937 State Department verifying Kobe-reported Japanese shipbuilding and mail-subsidy figures as unofficial but reliable.
